verses.1: I want you to know how much of a struggle I have on your behalf and on behalf of those in Laodicea and of all who have not seen my face in the flesh,
verses.2: so that their hearts may be comforted, knit together in love, and overflowing with the riches of full knowledge, to the understanding of the mystery of God, Christ,
verses.3: in whom are all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge hidden.
verses.4: I say this so that no one may deceive you with persuasive arguments.
verses.5: For even though I am absent in the flesh, I am with you in spirit and I rejoice and see your order and the firmness of your faith in Christ.
verses.6: So, just as you received Christ Jesus the Lord, walk in him,
verses.7: rooted and built up in him and established in your faith, just as you were taught, overflowing with gratitude.
verses.8: See to it that no one deceives you by philosophical arguments and empty deceptions, according to human traditions, according to the elements of the world, and not according to Christ;
verses.9: for in him the fullness of the godhead dwells bodily,
verses.10: and you are complete in him, who is the head of every rule and authority,
verses.11: in whom you were also circumcised with a circumcision not made with hands, by putting off the body of the flesh, by the circumcision of Christ,
verses.12: having been buried with him in baptism, in which you were also raised with him through faith in the energy of God who raised him from the dead,
verses.13: and when you were dead in your trespasses and the uncircumcision of your flesh, he made you alive together with him, forgiving us all our trespasses,
verses.14: having erased the certificate of debt that stood against us, with its legal demands; this he set aside, nailing it to the cross;
verses.15: having stripped the rulers and authorities and put them to open shame, triumphing over them in him.
verses.16: So then, let no one judge you in food or in drink or in respect of a festival or of a new moon or of the sabbaths,
verses.17: which are a shadow of what is to come, but the substance is of Christ.
verses.18: Let no one disqualify you, desiring to be humble and to worship the angels, gazing at things that have been seen, puffed up in his mind by his fleshly nature,
verses.19: and not holding fast to the head, from whom the whole body, through joints and ligaments, is nourished and knit together, growing in the increase of God.
verses.20: If you died with Christ from the elements of the world, why are you still living as if you were in the world?
verses.21: “Let no one touch, let no one taste, let no one handle,”
verses.22: referring to all things destined for destruction through human commands and teachings,
verses.23: which have the appearance of wisdom in self-imposed worship and humility and severity to the body, but are not of value in restraining the desires of the flesh.

notes:
Notes
- v. 23: The phrase "πλησμονὴς τῆς σαρκός" is translated as "restraining the desires of the flesh," preserving the contrast between external rituals and internal transformation.

[2] so that their hearts may be comforted, knit together in love, and overflowing with the riches of full knowledge, to the understanding of the mystery of God, Christ,
[3] in whom are all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge hidden.
[4] I say this so that no one may deceive you with persuasive arguments.
[5] For even though I am absent in the flesh, I am with you in spirit and I rejoice and see your order and the firmness of your faith in Christ.
[6] So, just as you received Christ Jesus the Lord, walk in him,
[7] rooted and built up in him and established in your faith, just as you were taught, overflowing with gratitude.
[8] See to it that no one deceives you by philosophical arguments and empty deceptions, according to human traditions, according to the elements of the world, and not according to Christ;
[9] for in him the fullness of the godhead dwells bodily,
[10] and you are complete in him, who is the head of every rule and authority,
[11] in whom you were also circumcised with a circumcision not made with hands, by putting off the body of the flesh, by the circumcision of Christ,
[12] having been buried with him in baptism, in which you were also raised with him through faith in the energy of God who raised him from the dead,

[14] having erased the certificate of debt that stood against us, with its legal demands; this he set aside, nailing it to the cross;
[15] having stripped the rulers and authorities and put them to open shame, triumphing over them in him.
[16] So then, let no one judge you in food or in drink or in respect of a festival or of a new moon or of the sabbaths,
[17] which are a shadow of what is to come, but the substance is of Christ.
[18] Let no one disqualify you, desiring to be humble and to worship the angels, gazing at things that have been seen, puffed up in his mind by his fleshly nature,
[19] and not holding fast to the head, from whom the whole body, through joints and ligaments, is nourished and knit together, growing in the increase of God.
[20] If you died with Christ from the elements of the world, why are you still living as if you were in the world?
[21] “Let no one touch, let no one taste, let no one handle,”
[22] referring to all things destined for destruction through human commands and teachings,
[23] which have the appearance of wisdom in self-imposed worship and humility and severity to the body, but are not of value in restraining the desires of the flesh.

- v. 23: The phrase "πλησμονὴς τῆς σαρκός" is translated as "restraining the desires of the flesh," preserving the contrast between external rituals and internal transformation.
